items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: I didn't have the pleasure of meeting him. But as I said, coming up in those river boat bands... I knew a lot about him.

ctx.x: I see Alphonso Trent with A. G. Gardner on drums, who was a sensation.

items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: He had A.C. Godley (Sensational) Gardley on drums. Alphonso Trent. Crook was his banjo player.

ctx.x: Yeah, you mention his band a lot. You must have really liked that man.

Certainly I did. He had A.C. Godley (Sensational) Gardley on drums. Alphonso Trent. Crook was his banjo player. He didn't play guitar in that band, he played banjo. Chester Clark, first trumpet player. Oh, yeah, a fellow was

telling me -- Arthur Hines, again, that he used to go -- Crooke finally settled in New York as a super in an apartment building. Say he used to go by and they'd play cards together. Crooke, banjo player formerly with Alphonso Trent. And good banjo player, rhythm-wise. Whatever way he played on the banjo. But it was good.

Wonderful. Only thing, I wasn't involved or interested in women, as most bandsmen do. All I wanted to do was to hear music, and I got some bands in my mind, Speed Webb, which I first heard Roy Eldridge. I don't know where Speed was from, I think around -- well, anyway, out in the Middle West or somewhere, Indiana or somewhere. McKinney's Kenny's Cotton Pickers, Zack White, Helvey's band. Oh, they were the swingingest bands in the land. Alphonso Alphonso Trent --
How did you end up going through Italy?
